what_its_for: Cabazitaxel is a cancer-fighting medicine (chemotherapy) used to treat prostate cancer that has spread to other parts of the body and has stopped responding to other hormone treatments. It works by slowing or stopping the growth of cancer cells.
how_to_take: This medicine is given to you by a nurse or doctor as an IV (intravenous) infusion directly into your vein. You will receive it in a clinic or hospital setting. Each infusion takes about 1 hour. You will also be given other medicines (antihistamines and steroids) at least 30 minutes before each infusion to help prevent allergic reactions. You should NOT try to give this medicine to yourself at home.
dosing: The typical dose is given once every 3 weeks (every 21 days). Your doctor will decide the exact dose based on your height, weight, and overall health. Your dose may be adjusted or your treatment may be delayed depending on how your body responds and any side effects you experience. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given in a clinic by a healthcare professional, it is very important that you keep all of your scheduled appointments. If you miss or need to reschedule your appointment, call your doctor's office or cancer care team as soon as possible to set up a new time. Do not try to make up a missed dose on your own.
storage: Cabazitaxel is stored and prepared by healthcare professionals in the clinic or pharmacy. You do not need to store this medicine at home. If you are given any other related medications to take at home, store them according to the label instructions and keep them out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid alcohol or discuss with your doctor before drinking. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as they can interfere with how this medicine works. Avoid close contact with people who have infections, colds, or the flu, since this medicine can lower your ability to fight infections. Avoid getting live vaccines (such as the flu nasal spray or shingles vaccine) while on treatment without asking your doctor first. Tell your doctor about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, as many can interact with cabazitaxel. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or confused.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room RIGHT AWAY if you experience: a fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher (this may be a sign of a serious infection); severe chills or shaking; signs of an allergic reaction during or after your infusion such as rash, hives, difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, or feeling faint; severe diarrhea or diarrhea with blood; severe stomach or belly pain; blood in your urine; unusual bleeding or bruising; extreme tiredness or weakness; shortness of breath; chest pain; numbness, tingling, or burning in your hands or feet; or signs of kidney problems such as very little urine output.
when_it_works: Cabazitaxel does not work overnight. It may take several treatment cycles before your doctor can tell if the medicine is helping. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular blood tests, scans, and check-ups. Even if you do not feel different right away, the medicine may still be working inside your body. Do not stop treatment without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and older): You may be at a higher risk for certain side effects such as infection, fatigue, and diarrhea. Your doctor will monitor you very closely. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have any kidney or liver issues. This medicine should be used with great caution or may not be recommended if your liver function is severely reduced. Your dose may need to be adjusted. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine can cause serious harm to an unborn baby. Do not use this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Men receiving this medicine should use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 3 months after the last dose. Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment and for 2 weeks after the last dose. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children.
